Investigated one question beyond the existing suites' own coverage: whether a record_write provenance-write failure (which occurs after the actual registry-document mutation in HumanPrincipalRegistryStore._write but before the capability's own consumption bookkeeping in record_write) could leave a formally-still-ACTIVE capability reusable for a second, distinct, successful mutation. No authority bypass is achievable. Disclosed as non-blocking finding F-1: a pre-existing, repair-unrelated availability/operability gap (the record wedges pending manual repair), not a security bypass, not introduced or altered by .1R.30R.3.2.1, out of this repair's own declared scope -- does not block N-16-5 closure. Also independently verified: registry strong-reference / object-ID-reuse structural safety (gc.collect does not evict an ACTIVE entry; the registry holds a strong reference for the life of each entry); _lookup_issued_capability checks record.capability is capability, not merely id() match; field mutation on genuinely-issued (non-shell) capabilities (subject/role/authority_class all rejected or ignored in the attacker's favor by registry dominance -- authority_class mutation has zero effect since the check compares record.authority_class, never writer.authority_class); registration-failure fail-closed (no capability escapes if issuance-record construction fails); validation-failure lifecycle (a rejected wrong-subject attempt does not burn the capability for its correct subsequent use); issuance-evidence document content directly inspected (no _authority_seal, no issuance_id, capability_identifier derivable only from operation_id); registry non-export (grep-confirmed, only hpac_foundation.py touches the registry) / issuance-function-inventory (AST-based: exactly the 3 expected functions, no clear/invalidate/deregister/reset helper) / consumer-boundary statics (no PAWA-module token in cli.py/commands/**/core/agent.py); fork/multiprocessing absence (no os.fork/multiprocessing/subprocess reachable from the PAWA module family; contract documents the admin tool as short-lived/one-operation, so fork is explicitly outside the trust model); concurrency-lock scope (the threading.Lock guards every registry mutation in all three helper functions) plus an independent 6-thread race (exactly 1 of 6 succeeds); the one pre-existing test-assertion change (.1R.30R.1 IV suite) confirmed strictly additive, not weakened, by direct diff inspection; historical .1R.30R.3.2 preserved byte-unchanged, STATUS: BLOCKED. not reopened or reinterpreted.
